title: Knowledge check: ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
options: ASP pages downloading instead of executing
questions.answer_key: ASP pages downloading instead of executing
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “ASP pages downloading instead of executing” under lesson 15, “ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Change several settings at once and infer which one fixed the issue.
Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
Assume every value from a browser is trustworthy.
Enable detailed errors for all public visitors.
questions.answer_key: Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps asp development environment troubleshooting testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
